issues.claim: W5.json enables[key="W6"]: "W6's mode-3 no-back-dating derivation needs a mint-side twin of NoPrematureTheftLock (a NoPrematureMintLock n rosterGen log := ...) plus the pinning theorem; W5 fixes the vocabulary j ≤ rosterGen (r / n) and provides the non-inductive per-window pinning lockstep_window_declares_rosterGen ... as the pin W6 would compose with. W6 should note that with a non-strictly-increasing counter the forward-stamp bound is NOT one grid window..."
issues.actual: docs/rollout/designs/W6.json (finalized, dated after W5's design) title: "No-back-dating derivation per mode: found NOT achievable additively under the current primitive shapes; text-only paper assumption plus a small Lean obstruction-witness recommended instead." Its own depends_on[key="W3a"].why states verbatim: "the planner's working hypothesis and the killed run-2 salvage both assumed W6 'must share a timed structure with W3a/W5'. This design finds that premise false for the item AS DELIVERED -- the two witness theorems use only the already-existing, timeless badSched/badKeyrotOn, not any timed stolenAt structure, so nothing here needs W3a to land first or to share any type with it." W6.json's enables array is empty, and grep of W6.json for NoPrematureMintLock/mint-side/rosterGen returns zero hits.
issues.fix: Delete or rewrite the W5.json enables->W6 entry: W6's finalized design does not consume LockstepPackageGen, badLockAt, or lockstep_window_declares_rosterGen, and explicitly disclaims needing anything from W5/W3a. A planner should not sequence W5 ahead of W6 on this basis; the entry should either be removed or annotated as superseded by W6's own (now-negative) finding.

issues.claim: W5.json enables[key="W4"]: "If W4 abstracts induction-over-syncs over a per-sync agreement lemma, it should parametrize the confirmation depth (d := n for modes 1-2, d := 2n for the mode-3 per-generation form) rather than hard-code n, or W5's headline cannot be plugged in later."
issues.actual: docs/rollout/designs/W4.json's structure SyncInductionData (n : Nat) already has a depth-agnostic per-step hypothesis `hStep : ∀ k, a k ∈ R (k + 1) → a (k + 1) ∈ R (k + 1)` with no hard-coded n or 2n anywhere in the abstract engine; W4.json's own new_theorems[reuse].why for SyncInductionData already notes it is "crypto- and protocol-free ... so a mode-3 lockstep per-generation induction (if one is wanted) could reuse the same structure and .invariant verbatim, supplying its own hStep from whatever lockstep per-generation agreement lemma W1/W5 produce."
issues.fix: Note in W5.json that W4's abstract engine already satisfies this by construction (opaque hStep, not hard-coded depth); the risk as phrased overstates a redo requirement that does not exist.

depends_on[W1] and enables[W1] in W5.json are mutually consistent with W1.json's own depends_on[W5] and enables[W5] entries (both mark the relationship soft/non-blocking and describe the same certificate-corollary composition in both directions) -- reciprocal cross-check passed.

Neither of W5's two depends_on entries (W1, W3a) is hard (both hard: false), and no other finalized design declares a hard dependency on W5 -- W5's own technical content (new files + two import lines) does not require any other work item to land first, and nothing else requires W5 to land first.
ordering_notes: W5 is additively self-contained: its only existing-file touches are the two root import-line additions permitted by docs/rollout/ROLLOUT_NOTES.md, it defines no field on any existing structure, and none of its six new files collide in path or declaration name with any of the other six finalized designs (W1, W2, W3a, W4, W6, W7 -- there is no separate W3b.json yet, it exists only as an unfinished designs-partial run). All of W5's depends_on edges are soft (hard: false) and reciprocally confirmed against W1's own design, so build order between W5 and W1/W3a is genuinely free, matching the design's own claim. The design would not need redoing if any sibling landed first, and no sibling needs redoing if W5 lands first -- with one caveat: three of W5's four `enables` entries turned out, on cross-checking against the other finalized designs, to overstate or misstate what the downstream item actually needs. The W6 case is the substantive one: W6's own finalized design (dated after W5's) explicitly investigated and rejected the premise that it shares any timed/stolenAt vocabulary with W5, delivering a negative/obstruction result instead. That does not force W5 to change, but a planner reading only W5.json would wrongly conclude W6 benefits from W5 landing first.
revised_effort: Unchanged from the design's own estimate (3-4 sessions) for the Lean work itself -- the ordering-lens findings are corrections to the depends_on/enables prose (a few sentences), not to the module/theorem plan, and cost only a few minutes to fix in W5.json.
